reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center and should not be counted in any assessment of Arizona AI infrastructure or grid load.

The listing is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product sold to small businesses in roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance. Its address in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County is currently occupied by a different company, TraVek Inc. Nothing publicly available connects the software business or that address to server infrastructure, colocation space, or dedicated data center equipment.

The entry exists because an OpenStreetMap point was tagged telecom=data_center, and the tag was carried into the dataset. No specifications are published for the site, and research is marked exhausted. The coordinates sit several miles from the other eight rows in the same batch, so no shared building links them. Each is an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro.

The useful signal here is about data quality, not capacity. A dataset of AI infrastructure will accumulate false positives wherever a volunteer map tag is treated as a facility. This row carries zero megawatts and no operator, which is the correct reading. It tells the reader nothing about Arizona's actual power or building constraints, and the state's published capacity figures come from other facilities entirely.
